verdict.rationale: E2B gives users direct control over the lifetime of sandbox data. Sandboxes can be killed at any time via SDK or CLI. Timeouts can be set and reset, acting as an automatic retention window. Paused sandboxes persist indefinitely until the user removes them, and self-hosting is available for full infrastructure control. However, none of the evidence frames this as a data retention or deletion policy, and nothing confirms that killing a sandbox purges its data. missing for 10: documented data retention policy, confirmation that kill/delete erases filesystem and memory data, deletion controls for snapshots and paused sandboxes, retention controls for logs/metadata held by E2B, independent corroboration.
